sections.content: How many people are "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services"?

21,960 people

were counted on the census as "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Managers and proprietors in this group co-ordinate the activities and resources of forestry, fishing, animal husbandry and related operations and establishments.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services", 14.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services" included:

  • property, housing and estate managers
  • personal assistants and other secretaries
  • barristers and judges

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services" there were more men than women (73.4% compared with 26.6%).

This means "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 73.4% and women made up 26.6% of "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services" included:

  • CAD, drawing and architectural technicians
  • physical scientists
  • senior police officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services", 10.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (76.7% compared with 23.3%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (56.3%) than an employee (43.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wiltshire, this is in the region of the South West.
